children: Investors' endless patience for big tech's AI spending spree is wearing thin. Look no further than shares of Alphabet today.

One key reason for the stock drop: Google's revenue from search advertising grew more slowly in the third quarter. That's in part because search queries in "AI Mode" were monetized at a lower rate than in traditional search, executives said.

Wall Street has signed off on big tech's massive artificial-intelligence spending spree partly because the core businesses are reliable money-making machines-making weakness in those areas an especially tough pill to swallow.
On top of that, Alphabet's free cash flow for the quarter dropped further into the red. It is only the second time the company has reported negative cash flow in its life as a public company.

When it comes to tech earnings, traders are a lot more demanding these days-and the market's bet on AI "is no longer a monolithic trade," said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services.
"With rates higher, the focus on profitability has risen," he said. "Investors want to see a vision and clear path to that." If left dissatisfied, Lerner said, they are "forcing discipline."
